newsitem.title: UK: East Europe, Mexico firm in emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: East Europe, Mexico firm in emerging debt market.

text.p: The emerging debt market was a little stronger on Wednesday but trading remains thin.
Firmer prices, after gains in New York the previous day, are essentially in line with a stronger U.S. long bond.
Traders said activity is unlikely to pick up before the U.S. consumer price number for February later in the day, which comes just under a week before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"The trend has been good across the board this morning. The market is a touch higher with the strength in Treasuries," a U.S. bank trader said.
There was very little action in Latin American paper, though Mexican par bonds MX625L19=RR were bid slightly higher.
But both Russia and Bulgaria rose, following the trend in other paper in New York.
The reorganisation of the Russia cabinet is expected to be completed next week.
But the sweeping changes so far, which have established a relatively young set of ministers in charge of economic reform, have been widely cheered in the market.
There was little fresh news out of Bulgaria but traders said the overall picture in the country has become far more positive after the agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
The deal at least means that Bulgaria wil be able to meet its Brady coupon payment in July, one trader said.
